verification_records.proposed_value: $72,480 CAD/year international upper-year rate (2026 entering cohort); annual increase applies only to new cohorts, not continuing students
verification_records.conflict_or_limitation_notes: Independent re-fetch of the Tuition Fee Report PDF (src-12) initially returned a DIFFERENT figure ($69,030) on two passes, which appeared to conflict with the extraction-pass's $72,480. Resolved by reading the table cohort-by-cohort: Table D2 prices EACH ENTERING COHORT's own locked-in upper-year rate separately. The 2023/2024/2025 cohorts all show $69,030 (unchanged across those years), while the 2026 cohort (the one this run's Program/CostProfile records represent) shows $72,480 -- and $72,480/$69,030 = 1.050, an exact 5.0% increase matching src-12's own 'approximately 5% annual increase for new cohorts' text precisely. This also resolves the prior annual_increase_note ambiguity: since three consecutive already-admitted cohorts all show the SAME rate while only the newest cohort shows a higher one, continuing students' rates are confirmed held flat, not re-priced annually. What initially looked like a new discrepancy was fully explained, not a genuine source disagreement -- records-v1.2.json's annual_increase_note field was updated accordingly. A fresh search this pass also located an IRCC study-permit proof-of-funds figure ($23,448 CAD, src-22) but it was deliberately NOT written into this CostProfile's living_cost_source_basis (that field's V1.2 kind enum excludes visa/immigration proof-of-funds figures by design) -- it is instead modeled as its own FinancialRequirement record; see vr-39.

RESOLVES vr-26's prior UNKNOWN. Three additional independent re-fetches of the same official Tuition Fee Report PDF this pass, reading it cohort-by-cohort rather than as a single flat table, converged on $7,610 as the 2026-entering-cohort's Year-1 non-Ontario-resident (NOR) Computer Science rate. This is corroborated by an internal ratio check: the confirmed Ontario-resident (OR) upper-year vs. NOR upper-year pair ($11,420 vs $14,260) has a premium ratio of 1.2487; pairing the confirmed OR Year-1 rate ($6,100) with $7,610 gives ratio 1.2475 -- essentially identical, strong internal evidence these two figures are the true paired Year-1 OR/NOR rates. The competing candidates from vr-26 are now explained rather than merely discarded: $14,180/$17,730 were traced this pass to a different row ('Bachelors', a general direct-entry category, not the Computer Science-specific program row) -- a genuine row-misattribution artifact of PDF-table extraction on this document, not an alternative true value for the same cell; $7,250 was traced to the 2025-entering-cohort's own (older) Year-1 NOR rate, distinct from the 2026 cohort's $7,610, consistent with NOR rates rising cohort-over-cohort while the government-regulated OR rate ($6,100) stays flat. tuition_annual is updated from null to $7,610 and record_status/verification_status are promoted to VERIFIED/VERIFIED accordingly. The corresponding NOR upper-year figure ($14,260, likely correct by the same logic) is NOT written to a canonical field, consistent with this run's convention of keeping upper-year steps in extension_metadata only, and because the 2026 cohort's own eventual upper-year rate has not yet been separately published (per the cohort-pricing pattern documented in cost-international's upper_year_tuition_step).
